question: Can revision-24 tolerant corrupt-tail fallback be made hostile-authoritative using only local footer validity, root placement, and prev ancestry?
causal_bound: An incomplete/uncommitted tail may contain a complete self-consistent generation payload+footer G' whose prev points at the prior committed footer P. The exact same observed bytes through G' are also a valid history in which G' was intentionally committed. No reader-only predicate over those bytes can recover external writer intent.
surviving_hardening: Read and validate the r24 header before scanning transaction footers.
Derive the canonical initial footer position from HDR.size + primary_csize + data_span + primary_csize.
Reject candidate footers physically before that canonical initial tail.
Allow prev=0 checkpoint authority only at the canonical initial footer and bind its payload hash to the header index hash.
Classify selection of an older valid footer with trailing bytes as best-effort prior-generation recovery rather than hostile-authoritative current state.
Keep arbitrary BMAGIC scanning heuristic; local CRC/SHA proves candidate content, not placement or commit membership.
Future dependency representations, including Issue26 backward-offset bases, may consume only authoritative committed ownership.
format_effect: None for confidence-tiering. Stronger authoritative recovery after arbitrary metadata/footer loss would require a future authenticated topology/chaining design or external trust.
